title: Cable Car Line 4 Will Be Ready in December 2027; “It’s a Social Justice Project,” Sheinbaum Says
author: Iván Evair Saldaña
content:
_This article by[Iván Evair
Saldaña](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Iv%C3%A1n%20Evair%20Salda%C3%B1a)
originally appeared in the [August 23, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/23/capital/linea-4-del-
cablebus-estara-lista-en-diciembre-del-2027-es-un-proyecto-de-justicia-social-
sheinbaum), Mexico’s premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. Cable Car (Cablebús) Line 4 “is a social justice project
because it is dedicated to giving those who have the least the best
transportation,” President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo maintained this Sunday,
during an inspection of the works at the Universidad station, near Ciudad
Universitaria. Accompanied by Mexico City Head of Government Clara Brugada,
the federal president reported that the project registers **20 percent
progress and is expected to be completed in December 2027**.

“The cable car is a mobility project that reduces travel times, is safe, and
helps —while you are on the route— to see the city from above, which calms
you, allows you to meditate, and keeps you out of traffic,” she stressed.

Cable Car Line 4 will connect the upper area of the Tlalpan borough with
Ciudad Universitaria, in the Coyoacán borough, in order to reduce people’s
travel time **from two hours to 40 minutes** , on average. Sheinbaum Pardo
also emphasized that it will help many students who commute daily to the
country’s largest university.

“Imagine, for the students who live in Tlalpan, even in Coyoacán, in the
Cantera area, well, it’s going to be very, very important to be able to get to
CU, and, moreover, here, well, it’s a transportation distribution hub
—trolleybus, metro, buses. So it’s an extraordinary idea, how the route of the
cable car was designed,” she noted.

For her part, the Head of Government pointed out that the three cable car
lines currently operating in the capital —driven, she stressed, by Sheinbaum
when she led the city government— make 40 million trips a year. Regarding the
new line, Brugada explained that it will have **nine stations along 11
kilometers, and will feature 390 cabins**.

> We deliver territorial justice, we deliver justice in time.
>
> Clara Brugada, Mexico City Head of Government

“It is estimated that from the highest point down to here, at the Universidad
metro station, it will be 40 minutes; travel times are cut by 50 percent, and
with that we deliver territorial justice, we deliver justice in time, because
it is those who live farthest away who spend the most time and the most
resources, and who today will be the beneficiaries. This project, as we know
—because what you did in the city is not new— fought inequalities, so it keeps
fighting inequalities,” she said.
